_comment: CANONICAL SOURCE OF TRUTH for the portfolio's projects. Facts mirrored from the PMO release wave (_pmo/assistant/release-wave-2026-07/COMBINED-NOTES.md). scripts/validate-projects.mjs FAILS the build when a content/projects/*.mdx drifts from this file (missing project, wrong repo/demo, stale pinned metric, banned brand string, or featured set mismatch). Edit facts HERE first, then the MDX prose to match. See MAINTENANCE.md.

cashflow-risk._demo: RETIRED 2026-07-29 and deliberately not replaced. The free Render Postgres expired 30 days after creation, so the app never bound its port and the edge hung for 75-120s. ADR 0003 in the repo records the options: $6/mo Render Basic (no spend authorised), a SQLite fallback REJECTED on architecture grounds with a do-not-re-propose clause, and — added by the 29 Jul amendment — Neon's free non-expiring Postgres, which would have worked and was declined on portfolio grounds rather than technical ones. Services are suspended, not deleted; the retirement is reversible. Until it is, this MUST stay null: the URL served a 503 'This service has been suspended by its owner' page, and a screenshot re-shoot captured exactly that.

cited-market-brief-agent._metrics: The '100% claims cited' pin was RETRACTED by the repo: the CI eval that produced precision 1.000 / recall 1.000 was built from the same rules that produced the output, so it could not fail. Measured against independently labelled ground truth: precision 0.579 dev / 0.400 holdout, recall 1.000. No precision figure is pinned as a metric chip on purpose — the repo's claim ledger requires the unit, positive class and population to be stated BEFORE the number, and a chip cannot carry that. The measured figures live in the write-up instead.

redteam-foundry._metrics: The '+1.00 cross-judge kappa' pin was WITHDRAWN by the repo: 11 of the 12 cells are degenerate 0/0 filled in by convention, so kappa there is undefined rather than perfect. The agreement claim now rests on the positive control (kappa = +0.935, n=98). A `headline_table.py --check` mode in the repo fails the build if the degenerate cells are reported as agreement — the banned strings below mirror that gate. NOTE: the withdrawn phrasing is deliberately NOT in `banned`. The write-up quotes it in order to retract it, and a string ban cannot tell an assertion from a retraction.

agent-release-gates._metrics: Pinned on the EXTERNAL result, not the in-corpus one. The repo's own README carries an [!IMPORTANT] block saying the synthetic benchmark is circular by construction and is not retrieval evidence, and the live dashboard leads with the same warning. The previous pins (safety recall 90.91%, side-effect block 100%) are both still numerically true, but the repo now records that the recall figure was measured with case-matching signals live and 'should not be read as a generalization estimate' — and a metric chip has nowhere to carry that caveat. THE TEST COUNT WAS DROPPED, NOT CORRECTED (Ross, 3 Aug 2026). It has been wrong at every single check — 305, 309, 309, 312, 317, the last two inside the same hour. A figure that decays faster than the page is edited is a liability rather than a fact, and the same count was removed from the upstream repository and from the CV for the same reason. It is replaced by gate mutation adequacy, which is a RESULT: 47.4% (9 of 19), 95% Wilson 27.3%-68.3%, 0 false positives over 4 benign controls. 47.4% AND NOT 52.6%: repairing the design defect the probe exposed moved the rate to 52.6% (10 of 19), but that is one discordant mutant at exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and docs/finding_gate_mutation_adequacy.md states plainly that it 'is not distinguishable from noise and is not claimed as an improvement in the rate'. The site pins the number its source stands behind.

marketing-effectiveness-lab._demo: RETIRED. The Streamlit URL answers 303 into a sign-in redirect loop that never reaches the app, so it is not publicly reachable. The repo agrees: its README calls the hosted surface one that 'may sleep or require access and is not an always-on public demo'. The GitHub Pages report at rosscyking1115.github.io/marketing-effectiveness-lab/ IS live and is the honest link for an archived project.
marketing-effectiveness-lab._headline: NO HEADLINE, deliberately. This project is archived, publishes no metrics at all, and has no "Honest limits" section — so there is no number to lead with and no evidence mode that would be true. The designer's mock filled the cell with "Bayesian / posterior layer", which is a phrase from the summary rather than a measurement, and put the ARCHIVED state on community-energy-flex instead (that project is shipped with a live demo). Marking the slot is the spec's own instruction where a fact is missing.

_mark: CANONICAL PROJECT MARK — the number shown in [ 05 ] on every surface. FROZEN, not computed. It used to be derived from a publishedAt-descending sort at render time, which meant the same project wore a different number in different places (home numbered within the lens, the index and the write-up numbered globally) AND that publishing a new project silently renumbered every existing one. IndexMark's own rule is that the mark is always TRUE, so a number that moves is a bug. Ross's call 2026-08-02: freeze at the values that were live, since all ten projects are finished. A new project takes the next free integer. NEVER renumber an existing one — the marks appear in screenshots, write-ups and the design spec.
_headline: HEADLINE NUMBER AND EVIDENCE MODE — the two authored cells in the /projects log, and the reason the log can be built without inventing anything. `metric` names a label that must exist in that project's MDX `metrics` array; validate-projects.mjs gates it, so the value itself is never duplicated here and cannot drift. `mode` is one of the design spec's three (§03 R5): CORRECTED (a published number was withdrawn and replaced), CONTROLLED (a null or negative result carried by a positive control), LIMITS (a result published with its documented limits). Every mode is grounded in a heading that already exists in the write-up — the spec is explicit that a correction is never fabricated to fill the slot. A null headline is DELIBERATE and must carry a _headline note saying why; it renders as a designed empty cell, not a gap. A CORRECTED headline must also carry `withdrawn` — the number it replaced — because §02 says a correction is shown as a struck pair, and half a correction is just a confident number. The withdrawn value is gated against the write-up body, so it cannot be invented: 0.24 → 0.42 (leakage audit), 99.31% → 79.92% (the benchmark was marking its own homework), 1.000 → 0.400 (the gate that could not fail). A CONTROLLED headline must also carry `control` — the metric its null result is measured against — because the spec renders that mode as "result vs control, side by side". A negative result with no control beside it is the thing redteam-foundry's own write-up says is meaningless: "a negative result only means something if the pipeline can detect a positive".
